findings.reason: The original standalone tile correctly renders the Definition but has no illustration. A control-flow picture materially clarifies the distinction between H-stage model recursion and execution of just the first selected action, with optional replanning rather than a prescribed update rule. This warrants an explanatory diagram under the expanded editorial scope.
findings.action: Added a final Remarks section with a four-stage directed flow and explicitly optional dashed return to planning.

correction: Added a source-justified TikZ MPC control-flow illustration and a notation/caveat paragraph in final Remarks; no original content or frontmatter changed.

diagram_math_checks.check: The plan node receives the finite learned model, s_0 in S, and H>=1; it initializes the real-valued function V_0 on S to zero and computes Q_h on admissible pairs and V_h on S for h=1,...,H.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Definition lines 34-36 gives exactly these inputs, initialization and recursion. def-learned-mdp-model Definition supplies finite nonempty state/action sets and probability rows; def-finite-horizon-mdp-return specifies the H-step undiscounted convention. The figure adds neither terminal reward nor discount.

diagram_math_checks.check: The selected a_0 lies in A(s_0) and satisfies Q_H(s_0,a_0)=V_H(s_0); first-listed tie-breaking is preserved.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Definition line 38 chooses the first action attaining V_H(s_0); the Remarks paragraph spells out the Q_H equality rather than treating V_H as an action. Finite nonempty A(s_0) and the maximum supplier justify attainment as already used by the Definition.

diagram_math_checks.check: The selector points to execution of only a_0 in the true environment, then observation of s_1 in S. No H-action open-loop execution or learned-model sample is depicted.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Definition line 38 explicitly distinguishes execution in the true environment from model planning and says the next state is observed. def-learned-mdp-model Definition puts the true and learned models on the same S and A(s).

diagram_math_checks.check: A dashed directed edge goes from observation back to planner input. Its label and prose identify a possible new invocation at s_1 with a supplied model; there is no model-update map or performance claim.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Definition line 38 says the controller may invoke again with new state and newly supplied model, and explicitly specifies no update rule or true-return guarantee. Returning to the planner means replacing its current-state input, not asserting s_1=s_0.

diagram_math_checks.check: Four process vertices, three solid forward edges (plan->choose->execute->observe), and one explicitly drawn dashed observe->plan return. All four arrows appear in the compiled native image, including the return segment into plan.east. No graph --cycle operation, geometric endpoint-open/closed convention, or commutative relation is involved.
diagram_math_checks.justification: The edges encode the order stated in Definition lines 34-38; the return is optional. The algorithm remains fully specified independently of the figure and no proof is inferred from it.
